BLOCKER: The mandated ordering predicate is not implemented: `gate_predicates.approval()` never compares `decision.at >= evidence.at`. Evidence now stores `at` (in `_ingest`) but nothing consumes it, so an approval recorded *before* a re-ingest of identical findings (or clock-skewed writes) is indistinguishable from a valid one — the AC's STALE_APPROVAL-by-timestamp case is unprovable.

Negative self-tests required by the AC are materially incomplete: `gate1_transition_check.py` has no self-test at all (missing design evidence / NO_EVIDENCE, missing Gate 1 decision, STALE_EVIDENCE unproven), and no test anywhere proves force-without-PF_GATE_FORCE is refused. Only 4 of the 6 mandated negative cases exist, all inside gate2.

Baseline governance is fail-open: `gp.baseline_problems()` findings (over-quota entries, missing reason/owner_item, >90-day `until`, malformed date) are printed in both `main()`s but never contribute to the exit code. A bloated or unowned baseline silently allows transitions/completions, contradicting "expired/unknown entries DENY" and fail-closed.
MAJOR: Decisions are not bound to an authenticated human. `by` is an unconstrained string, and neither `approval()` nor either checker validates it; `record_gate_decision(by="system:auto")` passes every gate. The force path even writes `by:"hil:forced"`. "Recorded only by the HIL session / never auto-approved" is convention, not enforcement.

Layering inversion: shipped control-plane `core/backlog.py` now imports `scripts/dev/architect_review.py` at call time and mutates `sys.path` inside functions. A library used by the backlog store depends on dev-tool path layout and availability; a missing/broken script turns every close into `GATE_ERROR`.

`item["decisions"]` is mutated via read-modify-write (`record_gate_decision`, force path) with no concurrency control or compare-and-swap. Two concurrent approvals or an approval racing a status write silently drops an append-only audit record while still leaving `seq` monotonic-looking.

docs-only/skip-glob logic is triplicated (`backlog._gate2_status`, `gate2_completion_check._docs_only`, size gate) with the same hardcoded default globs, and `_gate2_status` derives it from the *working tree* (`ar.changed_files()`) rather than the committed change set — the runtime predicate and the CI predicate can disagree, defeating the stated "local/CI cannot diverge" invariant.
MINOR: `_DESIGN_KEYS` is duplicated verbatim inside `_design_body`; the canonical hash and the reviewer-facing body can drift apart on the next field addition.
Force guard tests `os.environ.get("PF_CI")` truthiness, so `PF_CI=""` permits a forced close; should test key presence.
Decision `at` uses naive `datetime.now()` (no tz), which will make the required `at` ordering comparison unreliable across DST/timezones once implemented.
`record_gate_decision` accepts any `gate` value and silently maps everything ≠1 to diff mode; no allow-list of gates 1/2.

The decision-recording path uses `ar.gate_view(eid, "design")` while `gate1_transition_check` uses `gate1_check.evaluate` — two accessors for one predicate; the AC's single-predicate rule is only half-held.
NIT: `record_gate_decision` returns `None` for a missing item but the *unchanged* item on refusal — callers cannot distinguish "refused" from "no-op succeeded" without parsing stdout.
The CI/precheck gate invocation runs `--self-test` on every fast-tier run, adding steady-state latency for a matrix that rarely changes.
`gate-baseline.json` registered with `retention: "unbounded"` though it is a time-boxed rollout artifact that should be archived/emptied at rollout end.
SUMMARY: Structure is right (shared `gate_predicates`, fail-closed defaults, `--report`, docs-only handling, baseline file), but the implementation misses three explicit acceptance criteria: the `at`-ordering stale-approval predicate, the full negative self-test matrix (gate1 + force), and fail-closed baseline governance. Combined with unauthenticated `by`, sys.path-in-function imports in shipped core, and non-committed-tree docs-only detection, the gate can be satisfied by a stale or machine-authored approval while CI still passes — the audit trail is append-only in form, not in guarantee.
